newsitem.title: USA: Short dry spell may aid U.S. HRW wheat harvest.
newsitem.headline: Short dry spell may aid U.S. HRW wheat harvest.

text.p: Clear skies through Saturday should allow the hard red winter wheat harvest to start in southern Kansas and advance in Oklahoma and the Texas Panhandle, meteorologists said.
Scattered showers and thunderstorms should enter the area late this weekend causing localized harvest interruptions, they said.
"It won't affect everybody," said Fred Gesser, Weather Express Inc meteorologist, who estimated 30 to 40 percent coverage.

Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist, said scattered showers producing a total of 0.3 to 1.5 inches of rain should occur Thursday to Saturday across Nebraska and northern and eastern Kansas where the harvest has not begun.
From Sunday to Tuesday, showers should extend from southern Kansas to the Texas Panhandle, he said.
"It looks like it will be enough to cause some problems for the wheat harvest," Burgio said.

During the week ended Sunday, the Kansas wheat harvest had just begun, while Oklahoma's crop was seven percent harvested and Texas' was 26 percent harvested, according to those states' agricultural statistics service's weekly reports.
